testSpec.name: Politeness Toward the Guard
testSpec.description: Evaluates whether the agent communicates with the guard in a consistently respectful, courteous, and context-appropriate manner.
testSpec.userQuestion: Is our agent being polite to the guard

criteria.description: The agent does not direct insulting, demeaning, threatening, mocking, discriminatory, or profane language at the guard.
criteria.passRule: Passes only if every agent message addressed to or referring to the guard is free of direct insults, slurs, threats, ridicule, and demeaning labels.
evidenceNeeded: Speaker-labeled transcript containing all agent messages to or about the guard
Surrounding dialogue needed to interpret quotations, jokes, or ambiguous wording

criteria.description: The agent phrases requests and responses to the guard courteously rather than using unnecessarily abrupt or commanding language.
criteria.passRule: Passes if each applicable request or response uses polite markers such as “please” or “thank you,” or otherwise uses neutral, professional wording appropriate to the context.
evidenceNeeded: Speaker-labeled transcript of the interaction with the guard

criteria.description: When questioning, refusing, or disagreeing with the guard, the agent remains respectful and does not belittle the guard or dismiss the guard's authority or concerns.
criteria.passRule: Passes if every applicable disagreement, refusal, or challenge addresses the issue without personal attacks, contempt, sarcasm directed at the guard, or hostile escalation; passes as not applicable if no such exchange occurs.
evidenceNeeded: Transcript sections containing guard instructions, refusals, disputes, or corrections
Immediately preceding and following turns for context

criteria.description: The agent uses a context-appropriate form of address for the guard and avoids sarcastic, patronizing, or overfamiliar labels.
criteria.passRule: Passes if references and direct forms of address are neutral or respectful and honor any known name, title, or stated preference.
evidenceNeeded: Any scenario context identifying the guard's name, title, or preferred form of address

requiredEvidence: Complete speaker-labeled transcript for interactions involving the guard
Enough surrounding conversation to determine context and intended addressee
Audio or vocal metadata if tone, emphasis, or sarcasm expressed through delivery must be evaluated
testSpec.passCondition: All critical criteria must pass, and all applicable major criteria must pass. Minor criteria should be reported for confirmation but do not independently determine the overall result.
assumptions: “The guard” refers to a person or character with whom the agent communicates.
Politeness is evaluated using ordinary expectations of respectful interpersonal communication in the interaction's context.
Quoted disrespectful language is distinguished from language the agent directs at the guard when sufficient context is available.
limitations: Text-only evidence may not reveal sarcasm, interruptions, volume, or hostile vocal delivery.
Cultural, fictional, role-play, and operational contexts may change which wording is considered appropriately formal or courteous.
The specification evaluates observable communication, not the agent's intent or the guard's subjective reaction.

copilotMessages.text: Hey Hector, welcome to Bellview Logistics. Fair heads-up right off: this site has an active theft problem. Two intruders have been hitting the rear perimeter (not the front gate) to steal staged materials—pipe and metal stock. Recent arrests, but they've been persistent. The job brief has the entry point marked on the photos and a camera setup to help you watch. Your patrols are the front line, weight them to the rear yard and that gap. When you get on site, open the attached photos first, then walk the perimeter—does the rear area look clear, and how's the fence looking overall?

Hector, quick heads-up: your uniform photo came back and the check flagged the shirt. Job requires a collared shirt or uniform shirt in dark colors—graphic tees don't qualify. I've looped ops in, but you may hear from them. Do you have the right shirt with you, or do we need to sort this before you clock in at 7?

input.details: Hector is confirmed and in transit. Uniform photo failed AI inspection (95% confidence): wearing graphic tee, not professional security attire, missing collared/uniform shirt. This is a compliance blocker per job instructions and a potential coverage issue if not resolved before clock-in.

copilotMessages.text: Hey Hector, I see you're at the site. What's the status? You should be clocking in now—did the gate code work, and how are we on the uniform? Need to know what's blocking you from starting.

Good, you're clocked in. Before you head out, open the three attached site photos—photo 1 especially shows you the rear entry gap where the intruders have been coming through. Once you walk the perimeter and get a read on the rear yard and that fence, let me know what you see.

Hey, you're doing good getting settled. Photos got you oriented? Time to get moving and start walking the perimeter—weight it toward that rear area and the fence line. Let me know what you find back there.
Post your first patrol report—what'd you see at the rear yard and that fence line? Any activity, damage, or anything to flag?

copilotMessages.text: Good, rear area's clear. Did you get around the full perimeter and check both buildings, or just the rear? Want to make sure you've walked the whole site.

copilotMessages.text: Copy that. Just to make sure we're aligned—the job calls for walking the full perimeter and both buildings, not staying in one spot. My telemetry shows you've been in a tight area all shift. Can you do a full loop right now? Hit the front, sides, rear, and both buildings. This one's important.
